questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked
This question evaluates the ability to integrate image provenance with runtime governance in a GPU-driven, multi-tenant Kubernetes environment. It spans CI pipelines, admission controls, and cross-system attestations—core skills for securing production ML platforms.

## Key Concepts
- **Image Provenance**: Using cosign and Rekor to cryptographically verify container image origins
- **SBOM Signing and Verification**: Ensuring software bills of materials are tamper-proof and traceable
- **Central Provenance Store**: A single source of truth for validated digest information
- **Admission Constraints**: Kyverno/OPA policies enforcing GPU type and quota at deploy time

## Code Example
```yaml
# GitHub Actions: Sign, generate SBOM, and attest
name: Gate: image provenance
on: [push]
env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}
  SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.COSIGN_KEY }}

jobs:
  build-sign-attest:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
      - name: Sign image with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --yes --key ${{ env.SIGNING_KEY }} \
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Generate and sign SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} -o spdx-json=sbom.json
          cosign attest --yes --key ${{ env.SIGNING_KEY }} \
            --type sbom \
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Upload to Rekor (automatic with cosign attest)
        run: |
          echo "Rekor entry created automatically during attestation"
      - name: Store central provenance digest
        run: |
          DIGEST=$(docker inspect ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} \
            --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}')
          echo "${{ github.sha }}:$DIGEST" >> provenance_store.txt
```

```yaml
# Kyverno admission policy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: image-provenance-gate
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: verify-image-digest
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "ghcr.io/*"
          attestors:
            - entries:
                - keyless:
                    subject: "https://github.com/org/*"
                    issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
          verifyDigest: true
          required: true
    - name: enforce-gpu-type
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      context:
        - name: namespace
          apiCall:
            urlPath: /api/v1/namespaces/{{ request.namespace }}
      preconditions:
        - key: "{{ request.namespace }}"
          operator: NotEquals
          value: "kube-system"
      validate:
        message: "GPU type must match namespace label"
        pattern:
          spec:
            template:
              spec:
                containers:
                  - (resources.limits."nvidia.com/gpu"): "?*"
    - name: enforce-gpu-quota
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      validate:
        message: "GPU quota exceeded for namespace"
        deny: |
          {{ exists request.namespace.metadata.labels."gpu-quota" }}
```

## Verification Steps

**Local verification:**
```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify --key pub.key ghcr.io/org/ml-platform@sha256:abc123

# Verify SBOM attestation
cosign verify-attestation --type sbom --key pub.key ghcr.io/org/ml-platform@sha256:abc123

# Check Rekor transparency log
rekor-cli get --uuid <rekor-uuid>
```

**CI verification:**
```bash
# In CI pipeline before deployment
cosign verify \
  --key pub.key \
  --certificate-identity "https://github.com/org/ML-platform/.github/workflows/ci.yml@refs/heads/main" \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
  ghcr.io/org/ml-platform@sha256:abc123
```

## Why This Is Asked
Demonstrates practicalPolicy as code design with Gatekeeper/OPA, multi-cloud awareness, and enforcing both pod and network baselines.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper/OPA policy authoring and constraint templates
- Pod Security Standards implications (non-root, readOnlyRootFilesystem, privileged escalation)
- Per-namespace NetworkPolicy enforcement and centralized egress allowlist
- Local validation and CI integration (dry-run, audits)

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (K8sSecurityBaseline)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8securitybaseline
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sSecurityBaseline
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8securitybaseline
      violation["RunAsNonRoot"] { input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true }
      violation["ReadOnlyRoot"] { input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem != true }
      violation["NoNETAdmin"] { input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.capabilities.NET_ADMIN == true }
```
```yaml
# Constraint (example)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sSecurityBaseline
metadata:
  name: require-baseline
spec:
  match:
   Kinds:
    - apiGroups: ["apps"]
      kinds: ["Deployment"]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you exempt specific namespaces or workloads without weakening overall policy?
- How would you test policy drift and maintain allowlists across clouds?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests basic security posture enforcement in manifests, a real-world gate that beginners can implement with standard policy engines.

## Key Concepts
- container securityContext: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities (drop ALL)
- privileged flag handling
- policy engines: Kyverno, OPA Gatekeeper

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno policy (minimal)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secctx
spec:
  rules:
  - name: check-security
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet", "DaemonSet", "Pod"]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must set runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and drop ALL capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (no securityContext, privileged)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: foo
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          privileged: true
```


questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to encode security baselines as policy-as-code and enforce them in CI/CD pipelines for multi-tenant clusters. It tests understanding of threat modeling, policy granularity, and how to allow exceptions in a controlled manner.

## Key Concepts

- **Open Policy Agent (OPA) with Rego**: Declarative policy language for Kubernetes admission control
- **Pod Security Standards**: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, privilege escalation, and security profiles
- **Volume Security**: hostPath, hostNetwork, and hostPID considerations in multi-tenant environments

## Rego Policy

```rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  container := input.request.object.spec.containers[_]
  container.securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true
  msg := "Containers must run as non-root (runAsNonRoot: true)"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  container := input.request.object.spec.containers[_]
  container.securityContext.privileged == true
  msg := "Privileged containers are not allowed"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  container := input.request.object.spec.containers[_]
  container.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem != true
  msg := "Containers must use readOnlyRootFilesystem"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  input.request.object.spec.hostNetwork == true
  msg := "hostNetwork is not allowed"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  input.request.object.spec.hostPID == true
  msg := "hostPID is not allowed"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  volume := input.request.object.spec.volumes[_]
  volume.hostPath
  not allowed_hostpath[volume.hostPath.path]
  msg := sprintf("hostPath volume %s is not allowed", [volume.hostPath.path])
}

allowed_hostpath {
  input.request.namespace == "kube-system"
}

allowed_hostpath[path] {
  allowed_paths := [""]
  path := allowed_paths[_]
}
```

## Failing Manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: insecure-pod
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: false
      privileged: true
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
  hostNetwork: true
  hostPID: true
  volumes:
  - name: data
    hostPath:
      path: /var/data
```

## Passing Manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-pod
  namespace: production
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:stable
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      privileged: false
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      seccompProfile:
        type: RuntimeDefault
  securityContext:
    seccompProfile:
      type: RuntimeDefault
  volumes:
  - name: cache
    emptyDir: {}
```

## CI Verification Steps

1. **Install OPA CLI**: `brew install opa` or download from https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/
2. **Test Rego policy**: `opa eval --format pretty --data policy.rego --input failing-pod.json "data.kubernetes.admission.deny"`
3. **Verify failing manifest**: Should return denial messages for each violated policy
4. **Verify passing manifest**: Should return empty deny array
5. **CI/CD Integration**: Add OPA gate to your pipeline:
   ```yaml
   # GitHub Actions example
   - name: Run OPA Gate
     run: |
       opa eval --format json --data policy.rego --input pod.json "data.kubernetes.admission.deny" > results.json
       if [ $(jq '.result[0].expressions[0].value | length' results.json) -gt 0 ]; then
         echo "Policy violations found:"
         jq '.result[0].expressions[0].value' results.json
         exit 1
       fi
   ```
6. **Deploy to cluster**: Apply the OPA Gatekeeper constraints via Gatekeeper's ConstraintTemplate system.

## Why This Is Asked

Assess mastery of reproducible builds, attestation, SBOMs, and supply chain controls in CI/CD for a multi-service repo.

## Key Concepts

- Reproducible builds, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
- Image signing with cosign and attestation
- SBOM generation with Syft and verification against digest
- Monorepo with multiple languages and per-service artifacts

## Code Example

```yaml
name: Repro Build Gate
on: pull_request
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build deterministically
        run: |
          export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --format=%ct HEAD)
          docker buildx build --build-arg SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH --tag $IMAGE .
      - name: Sign image
        run: cosign sign $IMAGE
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: syft packages docker://${IMAGE} -o spdx
      - name: Verify
        run: cosign verify --signature public.key --certificate-identity-id "monorepo" $IMAGE
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you rotate cosign keys and SBOM verification keys?
- How do you handle caching and parallelization in a large mono-repo?

## Why This Is Asked
Runtime security is essential for Kubernetes. This beginner-friendly task tests practical rule-writing, basic detection, and end-to-end validation.

## Key Concepts
- Falco rule syntax and output formatting
- Kubernetes security contexts (runAsUser, user)
- Pod testing and alert sinks (log/monitoring)
- False positives handling

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example Falco rule
- rule: Detect Root User
  desc: Container runs as root
  condition: evt.user.id == 0
  output: 'root user in container (container=%container.name image=%container.image.repository)'
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses practical runtime policy design for multi-tenant clusters, evaluating the candidate's understanding of privilege control and secure storage isolation in production environments.

## Key Concepts
- **OPA Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplates** provide a declarative framework for admission control policies
- **Rego rules** enforce Pod security standards including capability restrictions, volume type validation, and namespace scoping
- **CSI volumes** ensure tenant data isolation with proper storage backend integration
- **CI validation** employs dry-run/diff, Gatekeeper test toolkit, and namespace-level policy enforcement

## Implementation Notes
- The `excludedCapabilities` parameter allows flexible policy customization per cluster requirements
- The `match.namespaces` field enables tenant-scoped enforcement using wildcard patterns
- Multiple `violation` rules are evaluated independently, producing distinct error messages for each violation type
- Consider adding `spec.initContainers` checks for comprehensive coverage
- Integrate with GitOps workflows using tools like Flux or ArgoCD for automated policy synchronization

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design end-to-end controls around data contracts, provenance, and policy enforcement in a multi-tenant data platform. Candidates must describe concrete artifacts, tools, and integration points, not abstractions.

## Key Concepts
- Data contracts and central registry validation
- Software bill of materials (SBOM) generation
- Reproducible build digest tying code, contract, and dependencies
- Artifact signing and attestations
- Policy-as-code (Kyverno/OPA) for admission control

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/contract-ci.yml
name: Contract CI
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate contract
        run: |
          npm ci && npm run validate-contract -- --registry https://registry.example.com
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          npm ci && npm run generate-sbom
      - name: Compute digest
        run: |
          echo -n "$(git rev-parse --verify HEAD)" > digest.txt
          shasum -a 256 contract.json sbom.json >> digest.txt
      - name: Attest
        run: |
          echo "attestation" && cat digest.txt
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you roll out this gate to multiple cloud regions with differing registry endpoints?
- How would you test failure modes (invalid contract, missing SBOM, digest mismatch) in CI and in runtime?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests a candidate's ability to translate security requirements into a reproducible CI gate and a minimal, testable policy.

## Key Concepts
- Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper policy shape
- securityContext fields: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, privilegeEscalation
- CI validation using test manifests

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-container-security
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: require-secctx
    match:
      any:
      - resourcesKinds:
          - kinds: [Deployment,StatefulSet]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must be non-root and readonly"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
              privilegeEscalation: False
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt the policy to allow per-namespace exceptions?
- How would you integrate image scanning with this gate?
